chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to a man a container (box), and there was wealth in the container. So the inheritors said, 'For you is the container, and whatever is in it is not for you'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The container along with whatever is in it, is for him'.
ai.seo_question: Does bequeathing a box include the money inside it according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal maxim that bequeathing a container implies bequeathing its contents unless explicitly excluded, a principle derived from common linguistic usage (urf). It highlights the Imam’s authority in resolving disputes between heirs and legatees by prioritizing the apparent intent of the testator over the literal separation of object and content. This ruling serves as a foundational precedent in Shia jurisprudence for interpreting wills and inheritance claims involving tangible assets.
